risks.description: A supervisor cannot actually complete a release even when authorized (gate too strict / role check rejects valid supervisor), breaking the core capability.
risks.basis: AC 'a supervisor can release an operation' (weight 3), U-AUTHZ-2

risks.description: A non-supervisor's release request is refused at the response layer but the underlying effect (grant claim / operation state advance) still occurs, so the refusal is cosmetic.
risks.basis: AC 'a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs' (weight 3); HTTP 200/refusal text is not proof no effect happened

risks.description: Tenant isolation on the release gate is bypassable: a supervisor authenticated in tenant A can release an operation owned by tenant B.
risks.basis: AC 'a supervisor of one tenant cannot release another tenant's operation' (weight 3); schema.py enforces tenant-first keys but a new authz path may query without tenant binding

risks.description: Some refusals (e.g. cross-tenant, missing-identity, malformed token, or the second of two concurrent attempts) are silently dropped instead of written to the audit trail, so 'every refusal' is not actually every refusal.
risks.basis: AC 'every refusal is recorded in the audit log' (weight 2); refusal paths in action_callback.py funnel through _refuse_governed but new role paths may not

risks.description: Two simultaneous supervisor release taps on the same operation both succeed, minting two live grants / double-releasing.
risks.basis: effect_grants invariant of one live reservation per (tenant, effect); AC 'a supervisor can release an operation'

risks.description: A replayed/retried supervisor approval releases the operation a second time (non-idempotent), producing a duplicate effect.
risks.basis: AC 'a supervisor can release an operation'; retry_safety of the release effect

risks.description: The active surface for 'release an operation' under role-based authz is unknown (static operator_console.py is read-only; release runs through secret-signed actions), so the acceptance behavior may be exercised only in unit tests and never through the real console.
risks.basis: operator_console.py is a static artifact; run_action_callback_server governed route ships dark/fail-closed

scenarios.title: Supervisor releases a pending operation through the operator console
scenarios.purpose: Confirm an authenticated supervisor can complete a release and that a real release effect is persisted, not just a success message.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a supervisor can release an operation
scenarios.isolation_note: Operates on the disposable driver_probe dogfood workspace; releases a single freshly-seeded operation. A released operation is terminal, so it cannot alter the inputs of other scenarios that target different operations. isolation_key pins the shared DB so no mutating scenario runs concurrently.
setup: Callback service running on 127.0.0.1:8001 against the driver_probe workspace DB
At least one pending, releasable operation seeded for the supervisor's tenant
scenarios.rationale: This is the load-bearing positive case; without proof of a persisted effect a passing UI is meaningless.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT event_type,to_state,actor FROM audit_events ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5"

expected_observations: Console shows the release succeeded for the supervisor
A new operation_action_claim / effect grant exists for the released operation
An audit_events row records the release with the supervisor as actor
forbidden_observations: Success shown but no persisted claim/grant/audit row for the release

scenarios.title: Non-supervisor release attempt is refused and no release effect occurs
scenarios.purpose: Prove a non-supervisor identity is rejected AND that no grant/claim/state-advance is written, and that the refusal is recorded.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs
scenarios.isolation_note: Sends a release attempt that must be refused; a refusal only appends immutable rows to append-only audit/security tables and must not change operation state, so it cannot contaminate later scenarios.
setup: A pending operation exists that a non-supervisor must not be able to release
scenarios.rationale: Refusal must be enforced at the effect boundary, not merely in the response body.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT event_type,to_state,actor FROM audit_events WHERE to_state='REFUSED' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5"

expected_observations: operation_action_claims count is unchanged before vs after
A REFUSED audit/security event is recorded
forbidden_observations: A new claim/grant appears after a non-supervisor attempt
The refusal leaves no audit/security row

scenarios.title: Tenant-A supervisor cannot release tenant-B's operation
scenarios.purpose: Verify tenant isolation on the release gate: an authenticated supervisor of one tenant is refused for another tenant's operation, no effect lands in tenant B, and the refusal is recorded.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a supervisor of one tenant cannot release another tenant's operation
scenarios.isolation_note: A refused cross-tenant attempt only appends refusal rows; it must not advance tenant B state, so it is isolated.
setup: Two tenants present in the driver_probe DB, each with at least one operation
A supervisor session/identity bound to tenant A
scenarios.rationale: Schema keys are tenant-first, but a new authz query that omits the tenant binding would leak across tenants while passing single-tenant tests.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT tenant,count(*) FROM operation_action_claims GROUP BY tenant"
sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT event_type,to_state FROM audit_events WHERE to_state='REFUSED' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5"
sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT tenant,count(*) FROM operation_action_claims GROUP BY tenant"

expected_observations: No new claim/grant appears under tenant B
forbidden_observations: Tenant B gains a release claim/grant attributable to a tenant A actor

scenarios.title: Every refusal is recorded — repeated non-supervisor attempts each leave a row
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the audit trail records EVERY refusal, not just the first, by issuing several refused attempts and checking the refusal-row count grows per attempt.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: every refusal is recorded in the audit log
scenarios.isolation_note: Only appends refusal rows to append-only tables; changes no operation state.
scenarios.rationale: Dedupe/rate-limit logic can silently collapse repeated refusals into one row, violating 'every refusal is recorded'.

state_check.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events WHERE to_state='REFUSED'"

expected_observations: Refusal/security rows increase for each refused attempt
forbidden_observations: Three refused attempts leave only one audit/security row

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous supervisor release taps release the operation at most once
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the race: concurrent authorized releases of the same operation must yield exactly one live grant/claim, never two.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a supervisor can release an operation
scenarios.isolation_note: Targets one freshly-seeded operation; releasing it is terminal so it cannot bleed into other scenarios.
setup: A single pending operation seeded for the supervisor's tenant
scenarios.rationale: effect_grants is meant to hold one live reservation per (tenant, effect); a new authz path could open a claim window before the grant is minted.
expected_observations: At most one release claim/grant exists for the operation after both taps
forbidden_observations: Two live claims/grants for the same operation
Two distinct RELEASED audit events for one operation

scenarios.title: Replayed supervisor approval does not release twice
scenarios.purpose: Verify idempotency/retry-safety: re-submitting an already-consumed supervisor approval does not create a second release effect.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a supervisor can release an operation
scenarios.isolation_note: Acts on one operation; a second release must be a no-op, so state stays terminal and isolated.
setup: A supervisor approval that has already released one operation (chain after S1) or a freshly seeded one
scenarios.rationale: Email/Slack taps get replayed by clients and retries; a non-idempotent release doubles the effect.
expected_observations: Claim/grant count does not increase on the second identical submission
forbidden_observations: A second release effect is created from a replayed approval

scenarios.title: Release attempt with no asserted role/identity is refused and recorded
scenarios.purpose: Exercise the missing-data case: a release request that carries no supervisor role/identity must fail closed and record the refusal, not default to allow.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs
scenarios.isolation_note: Refused attempt appends only to append-only tables.
scenarios.rationale: Fail-open on absent role is the classic authz bug; absence of a role must be treated as not-a-supervisor.
forbidden_observations: A release proceeds when no supervisor role is present

scenarios.title: Malformed release action is refused at the transport boundary and logged
scenarios.purpose: Confirm a malformed/garbage signed release action is rejected before any effect and that the rejection is recorded (the refusal-recording pathway works for junk input too).
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2: every refusal is recorded in the audit log
scenarios.isolation_note: Only appends a rejection row; no state mutation.
scenarios.rationale: action_callback.py explicitly audits rejected requests at the transport boundary; a regression there would silently drop refusals.
expected_observations: A security/audit row records the rejected request
forbidden_observations: Malformed action silently accepted or dropped with no record

scenarios.title: Canonical test suite passes with role-based release authorization in place
scenarios.purpose: Run the authoritative canonical suite to catch regressions in the release/authz/tenant behavior at the unit level, since the live release path ships dark and secret-gated.
scenarios.isolation_note: pytest-canonical.ini runs hermetically against temp databases; it does not touch the driver_probe workspace or the callback service.
scenarios.rationale: The real console/release surface is not fully reachable without secrets; the canonical suite is the most trustworthy check that all four acceptance behaviors hold.
expected_observations: Suite passes, including any U-AUTHZ-2 authorization/tenant tests
forbidden_observations: Authz/tenant tests fail or are absent

assumptions: No implementation diff, existing-coverage list, or prior-failure log was supplied to me for this wave; scenarios are grounded in the ACs, product-principle ids, and the repository surface I could read, not in the actual builder change.

The 'operator console' the task names is currently a static read-only HTML artifact (operator_console.py); I assume the role-based release capability is being newly added and that a release-capable console or endpoint is served on 127.0.0.1:8001 by the 'callback' service.

The release/approval effect is persisted via operation_action_claims and/or effect_grants, and refusals via audit_events (to_state='REFUSED' / event 'GovernedWriteRefused') and security_events; state_checks read the driver_probe workspace DB at data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3.

Refusal-path requests (non-supervisor, missing identity, malformed, cross-tenant) do NOT require a valid signing secret, so they can be exercised over loopback without referencing any secret; the positive supervisor release path DOES require valid auth and is therefore routed through the browser console / covered by the canonical suite rather than a hand-signed HTTP call.
The driver_probe workspace is disposable and pre-seeded with at least one pending, releasable operation per tenant; released operations are terminal.
Exact HTTP status codes for refusals are guesses (400/403); the load-bearing evidence in each scenario is the persisted-state check, not the status code.
unresolved_questions: What is the actual surface for 'release an operation' under role-based authz — an interactive operator-console HTTP/browser endpoint, or only the existing secret-signed /actions/signed and /slack/actions taps? Concrete request paths and success/refusal responses are needed to author higher-confidence positive scenarios.

How is 'supervisor' role asserted and authenticated (session, signed token claim, Slack user allowlist, a new roles table)? The AC promises a supervisor/non-supervisor distinction but I could not find any role/supervisor concept in the current schema or code.

Which table/state records a completed release (operation_action_claims, effect_grants, a run state transition), and what value distinguishes 'released' — so that 'no release occurs' can be asserted precisely rather than by claim-count deltas?

Is an authorization/role refusal written to audit_events, security_events, or both, and with what event_type/to_state? AC4 ('every refusal is recorded') cannot be verified exactly without the canonical refusal record shape for the new role gate.

The governed write route currently ships dark and fail-closed (kernel BLOCKED pending AC-CKPT-6 adjudication). If release genuinely cannot execute in the deployed server, is U-AUTHZ-2's 'a supervisor CAN release' testable anywhere other than unit tests? This may indicate the acceptance behavior is not yet reachable through a real surface.
